preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism relies on a built-in encoder and PID algorithm to dynamically adjust the rotational speed, but it fails to address the root cause of the imbalance vibration, which is the rotor's inherent design and manufacturing tolerances. The evidence from [doi:10.1177/1077546304035603] Dynamic Balancing of a Centrifuge: Application to a Dual-Rotor System with Very Little Speed D shows that even with advanced balancing techniques, rotor imbalance can still occur due to manufacturing defects.

The candidate's proposed solution assumes a fixed rotational speed of 15000 rpm, but the boundary conditions of the problem statement specify that the rotor assembly operates at speeds above 4000 g, which is a non-linear and dynamic condition. The evidence from [doi:10.1016/0022-460x(82)90319-4] Non-linear effect in high speed rotor noise shows that non-linear effects become significant at high speeds, making the proposed solution inadequate.

The candidate cites [doi:10.1016/j.ohx.2025.e00694] Centrifugal device for dust adhesion measurement as evidence of the effectiveness of the proposed solution, but this paper actually discusses a different application and does not provide any data or analysis relevant to the problem of rotor imbalance vibration. This contradicts the candidate's claim of using relevant evidence to support their solution.

The candidate's proposed solution is essentially equivalent to the baseline condition, which is the current implementation of the benchtop high-speed laboratory centrifuge rotor assembly. The proposed solution does not introduce any new design variables or mechanisms that would improve the performance of the rotor assembly beyond the current state-of-the-art. The candidate's proposed solution requires the integration of an encoder and PID algorithm into the existing motor controller, but this would require significant hardware and software modifications, which are not feasible given the constraints of the problem statement. The evidence from [doi:10.1002/cpz1.70454] Bacterial Lysis Observation Over Time Assay (BLOTS) for High-Throughput Isolation, Sequencing, and Characteriz shows that even with advanced software and hardware, the integration of new components can be challenging and may not be feasible in practice.
